subject: Prod: sudden quality & p99 latency regression after v4.2-quant
messages:
From: Ana Costa <ana@paycore.com>

Date: 2028-09-03T13:22:00Z
Subject: Production: spike in p99 and hallucinations after v4.2-quant

Hi Mina,

We rolled the v4.2-quant variant at 11:45 PDT and within ~30 minutes we started seeing 3x p99 latency on our embed+generate path and a sharp increase in nonsense completions for payment-related prompts. Error rate (500s) climbed from 0.2% to 1.6%. This is impacting checkout flows — we had to failover to an older region for some sessions.

Attached is a small sample of requests (+ timings) and a short screencap of the spike. Can your team triage? We need a rollback plan if this can't be fixed within the hour.

Attachments:
- paycore-sample-requests.ndjson (50 requests)

Thanks,
Ana Costa

Date: 2028-09-03T13:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Production: spike in p99 and hallucinations after v4.2-quant

Forwarding PayCore's samples. High priority — customer is seeing p99 ~3x and increased 5xxs immediately after v4.2-quant rollout.

What I need from the infra/runtime side:
- Rishi: check qprofile diffs between v4.1-quant (gold) and v4.2-quant, look for any layer-level quantization shifts or dtype fallbacks. Prior incidents were caused by an unexpected int8 path on attention kernels.
- Grace: verify batch queue sizes, per-worker in-flight counts, and whether autoscaler/traffic split caused hot shards.
- Marcus: surf logs for OOM/retries and measure token decode latencies per-worker.

Attachments I'm uploading to the incident folder: debug_payloads.tar.gz, qprofile-diff.csv, runbook-rollback.md

If the analysis indicates a quant profile regression, we will recommend an immediate rollback to v4.1-quant. If it's a routing/hot shard issue, we may push a short-lived routing policy to spread traffic.

—Mina
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-03T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: spike in p99 and hallucinations after v4.2-quant

Quick summary of what I found so far (local repro on customer's sample):
- The v4.2-quant build introduced a slightly different per-layer scale which caused two attention layers to take a slower float path on A100s with the latest kernel set; this increases decode latency non-linearly at high concurrency.
- KV cache memory growth: the quant encoding changed tensor shapes for some legacy prompts, leading to a 12% larger KV footprint for the sample set; that pushes some workers into more GC/retry cycles.
- There are intermittent tokenization mismatches on rare payment tokens (0.3% of cases) — explains some hallucinations.

Immediate mitigation options (ordered):
1) Roll back to v4.1-quant variant (fast, high confidence) — we can flip traffic in <10 minutes and confirm metrics within 5 minutes.
2) Apply a temporary kernel fallback at runtime forcing stable attention kernel (risky, takes 20–30m, needs careful testing).
3) Adjust autoscaler to increase spare workers + throttle batch caps (less ideal; customer-facing latency may still spike until KV growth stabilizes).

I recommend rolling back now while we fix the qprofile diff in parallel. I'm attaching a short diff (`qprofile-diff.csv`) and a proposed rollback runbook.

—Rishi
Lead Infra SRE
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production: spike in p99 and hallucinations after v4.2-quant

Ana — we have a recommended plan: immediate rollback to v4.1-quant now, then a post-mortem to remediate the qprofile change.

Plan of action (start in ~5 mins):
- Step 1: Roll traffic to v4.1-quant across PayCore's region (expected flip <10m).
- Step 2: Monitor p95/p99, 5xxs, and hallucination sample set; we'll report in 5m and 15m increments.
- Step 3: If metrics do not recover, we will put the incident into P1 escalation with an executive hook.

We'll execute the rollback now and follow up with screenshots and metrics. I will also share an incident ticket with the timeline and retention of logs.

Attachments: runbook-rollback.md

—Mina

Subject: Executive note — PayCore degradation and remediation

Ana — I'm Evelyn (VP, Customer Success). We saw Mina's rollback and Rishi's analysis — thank you for the sample data, it accelerated our triage.

We're committed to a post-incident review and a specific remediation plan to prevent future qprofile regressions. Short term: we will provide a one-month service credit for the impacted windows and a prioritized engineering patch for the quant profile validation pipeline.

I'll set up a 30-minute post-mortem with our engineering leads and PayCore stakeholders for tomorrow to review root cause, tests we will add, and an expected delivery date for the fix.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll stay on this until you're back to baseline.

—Evelyn Hart
